intro.heading: The whole picture, in one place
intro.body: Diagnosis day hands you a flood of new names, new appointments, and new instructions, all while you're least able to hold onto any of it. This won't manage your care for you — that's what your doctors and care team are for — but it gives every appointment, medication, symptom, test result, approval, call, and bill one calm, private place to live. It works the same way whether it's your diagnosis or you're the one holding it together for someone else.

privacy.heading: Private by design, not by promise
privacy.body: Nothing you type is ever sent anywhere — it's saved only in this browser, on this device. That also means anyone who can use this device and this browser can open it: it isn't encrypted or password-protected, so keep it somewhere only you can reach, and think twice before putting a full member ID or account number in it if the device is shared.

cards.title: Zero network requests
cards.body: The app is a single file that runs entirely in your browser, on your device. It makes no connections and loads nothing from the internet. You can run it with Wi-Fi off.

cards.title: Never a password
cards.body: By design, it never asks for or stores passwords or PINs. It records that accounts exist and where your written instructions live — the map, never the keys.

cards.title: Yours forever
cards.body: One-time purchase. The file is yours, works offline for life, and will still open years from now, exactly as it does today.

priceCard.sub: the one private place to keep track of a serious diagnosis — appointments, medications, symptoms, test results, approvals, records, calls, and every bill — whether you're the patient or the one holding it together for them, so nothing gets lost in the blur of the first weeks and every visit starts with the picture already organized.
bullets: 37 guided tasks across six phases: Get Oriented, Before Treatment Starts, Track Care as It Happens, Medications & Symptoms, Money as It Arrives, Before Each Visit
An appointment & treatment tracker — provider, what happened, and the next step for every visit, hospital stay, and procedure
A medication register with dose, prescriber, purpose, and the date each one started or last changed
A symptom & side-effect log that records what you're noticing, never what it means, with a place for the treatment cycle and day
A test result log — what test, what you were told, and whether it's filed or pending
A running, checkable list of questions for the doctor, so nothing gets forgotten in the exam room
An approvals & referrals tab for anything waiting on approval, with its reference number and the date it's good through
A records tab for which pathology report, slide set, or imaging disc you actually hold and which you've asked for
An insurance claim & EOB tracker — date of service, claim number, billed, insurer paid, what you owe, and a running total of what you've actually paid
An other-costs tab for mileage, parking, lodging, and everything else that never shows up on an EOB
A calls tab for who you spoke with, what you were told, and the reference number they gave you
A care team tab for everyone treating you, in one place
Two one-click printables: a Visit Summary for your next appointment, and a separate Money & Coverage Summary for a billing call

faq.q: Do I need to install anything?
faq.a: No. You download a small file, double-click it, and it opens in the browser you already use — on Mac, Windows, tablets, and phones.
Yes, structurally. The app makes zero network requests — you can verify this with Wi-Fi turned off. Your entries live only on your device, and your backup is a file you control.

faq.q: What if it doesn't work for me?
faq.a: Email hello@quietkeep.co and we'll make it right. We answer every message.

crossSell.heading: Caring for an aging parent day to day?
crossSell.body: Ninth Quietkeep organizer and the first in the medical-crisis lane. This product serves the patient and the person organizing care for them equally — the caregiver need is met inside the file, not deferred elsewhere. Where it genuinely leads on is different: a long illness that becomes ongoing day-to-day care for an aging parent points to the Caregiving Companion, and if a diagnosis turns terminal, the Estate Planning Organizer is the right next thing — handled with care in messaging rather than in-app logic, and never surfaced from anything the buyer types.
